messages.subject: Graph specifics
parts:
I'm trying to figure out why the axis, the breaks/labels aren't
exactly the same between the data. I want them all to look alike.


g <- ggplot(txdata, aes(x=gcsf_dse4, y=gcsf_dse4_IBW)) +
geom_point(shape=1, colour="blue")
g <- g + scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(0, 25, 5), expand=c(0,0))
g <- g + scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(0, 50, 5), expand=c(0,0))
g <- g + coord_cartesian(xlim=c(0, 25))
g <- g + coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0, 50))
g <- g + theme_bw()
png(filename="Figure5.png", width=720, height=480)
g
dev.off()




g <- ggplot(txdata, aes(x=gcsf_dse5, y=gcsf_dse5_IBW)) +
geom_point(shape=1, colour="blue")

g <- g + scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(0, 50, 5), expand=c(0,0))
g <- g + coord_cartesian(xlim=c(0, 25))
g <- g + coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0, 50))
g <- g + theme_bw()
png(filename="Figure6.png", width=720, height=480)
g
dev.off()

messages.subject: Re: Graph specifics
parts:
Rachel, 

If you had included some dummy data it would have been easier to get started... 

library(ggplot2)
txdata<-data.frame(gcsf_dse4 = rnorm(10000, 15, 7), gcsf_dse5 = rnorm(10000, 15, 5), gcsf_dse4_IBW = rnorm(10000, 25, 20),  gcsf_dse5_IBW = rnorm(10000, 25, 10))
#on different lines, it ignores the xlim
ggplot(txdata, aes(x=gcsf_dse4, y=gcsf_dse4_IBW)) +
geom_point(shape=1, colour="blue") +
scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(0, 25, 5),  expand=c(0,0)) +
scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(0, 50, 5),  expand=c(0,0)) +
coord_cartesian(xlim=c(0, 25)) +
coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0, 50)) +
theme_bw()
#on the same line, both coordinates are observed correctly
ggplot(txdata, aes(x=gcsf_dse4, y=gcsf_dse4_IBW)) +
geom_point(shape=1, colour="blue") +
scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(0, 25, 5),  expand=c(0,0)) +
scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(0, 50, 5),  expand=c(0,0)) +
coord_cartesian(xlim=c(0, 25), ylim=c(0, 50)) +
theme_bw()

I noticed the issue when I was playing with coord_cartesian(). When you set the xlim and ylim on different lines of your code, you are overwriting the previous line with the default (NULL it seems). If you put them on the same line, it adheres to your limits in both directions. 

Brandon

They seem to line up to me. 

library(gridExtra)
library(ggplot2)

txdata<-read.csv("~/Downloads/rf_prop141007.csv", header=T)

a <-
ggplot(txdata, aes(x=gcsf_dse4, y=gcsf_dse4_IBW)) +

geom_point(shape=1, colour="blue") +
scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(0, 25, 5),  expand=c(0,0)) +
scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(0, 50, 5),  expand=c(0,0)) +
coord_cartesian(xlim=c(0, 25), ylim=c(0, 50)) +
theme_bw()

b <-
ggplot(txdata, aes(x=gcsf_dse5, y=gcsf_dse5_IBW)) +

geom_point(shape=1, colour="blue") +
scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(0, 25, 5),  expand=c(0,0)) +
scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(0, 50, 5),  expand=c(0,0)) +
coord_cartesian(xlim=c(0, 25), ylim=c(0, 50)) +
theme_bw()

png("xalign.png")
grid.arrange(a,b)
dev.off()

png("yalign.png")
grid.arrange(a,b, ncol=2)
dev.off()

I'm not sure what else is going on that they aren't working for you. 

Brandon
